# 

::: {.title}

Early Positive School Perspectives of Criminality

:::

# 

![](Images/muhaha.png){fig-align="center"}

## Positivism (Early 1900s)

:::{.small-text}



[A framework that uses scientific methods to understand criminal behavior by focusing on biological or psychological elements, rather than free will]{.blue}. 

<br>

Behavior is determined by [measurable causes, not just individual choice]{.blue}

<br>

Each framework (biological, psychological) had a distinct individual influence on crime

<br>

Replaced the Classic School (e.g., Rational Choice Theory)

:::

::: notes

Moving away from free will, classical theories to more scientific method centered. 

Which in the early 1900s the scientfic method was really a hot topic, with the Industrial Revolution had already shown how applying science and technology could transform economies and daily life.


:::


## Pseudoscience

[A collection of beliefs or practices mistakenly regarded as being based on scientific method or evidence.]{.blue}

<br>

[Characteristics:]{.blue2}

<br>

1.) Lacks empirical support or testability.

2.) Relies on [anecdotal evidence or subjective validation]{.blue}.

3.) Often resistant to criticism or revision.

<br>

For example, Astrology and [Scientology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientology)

# EVERYTHING YOU ARE ABOUT TO HEAR IS A PSEUDOSCIENCE!

## Eugenics 

:::{.small-text}

The study and implementation of [policies aimed at improving the human race through controlled reproduction, often enforced on specific groups.]{.orange}

Individuals were classified into "superior" and "inferior" groups based on perceived genetic traits.

Linked criminal behavior to heredity and [advocating for selective reproduction to reduce crime.]{.blue}

:::



![](Images/CSH.jpg){fig-align="center"}




::: footer

image: Cold Spring Harbor

:::


## Positivism, Eugenics, and Nazi Germany


:::{.smaller-text}

Applied positivist ideas to “improve” society through controlled reproduction, sterilization, and eventually genocide

<br>

[Nazi Germany (1933–1945)]{style="text-decoration: underline;"}

[Law for the Prevention of Hereditarily Diseased Offspring (1933):]{.blue}
Mandated the forced sterilization of individuals diagnosed with certain hereditary conditions (e.g., schizophrenia, epilepsy, hereditary blindness, serious deformities, chronic alcoholism).

<br>

The law institutionalized eugenics courts and provided the legal framework for large-scale sterilization programs. 

<br>

Culminated in mass sterilizations, euthanasia programs, and the Holocaust


:::

## Positivism and Slavery in the U.S.

:::{.small-text}

[Scientific Racism]{.blue} 

Positivist “measurements” (skulls, faces, bodies) misused to prove racial hierarchies


<br>


[Biological Determinism]{.blue}

The theory that biological factors, primarily genetics and physical traits, determine human behavior, social structures, and cultural norms


<br>

[IQ Testing]{.blue} 

Misapplied to reinforce stereotypes of Black intellectual inferiority and justify discriminatory policies

:::

## How Positivist Claims Were Propagated with Pseudoscience

:::{.small-text}

[Craniometry]{.blue} measuring skull size/shape to “prove” intelligence or criminality

<br>

[Physiognomy]{.blue} judging moral character from facial features

<br>


[Misuse of Darwin’s On the Origin of Species]{.blue} distorted into “Social Darwinism,” justifying racial hierarchies and eugenics

<br>

[IQ Testing]{.blue} misapplied to label groups as “feebleminded” or criminal, used to support sterilization policies

:::

## Craniometry



:::{.small-text}

The study of [skull and brain size as indicators of superiority or inferiority among individuals or racial/ethnic groups.]{.blue}

Skull size and shape were believed to reflect brain capacity, [with larger skulls indicating higher intelligence and moral superiority.]{.orange}

Used to justify racial hierarchies and discriminatory policies that [linked traits to criminal behavior.]{.blue2}

:::



![](Images/cran.jpg){fig-align="center"}

::: footer

Image: Science Photo Gallery

:::



::: notes

It was believed that the skull's size and shape perfectly reflected the brain's structure and capacity, with larger skulls indicating greater intelligence and moral superiority.

:::

## Where We’ve Been in Module 1

:::{.smaller-text}

[Pre-Classical Theories]{.blue}

Crime explained through spiritualism, absolute good vs. absolute evil

<br>

[Classical Theories]{.blue}

[Introduction of free will]{.blue2}

Rational choice & deterrence as central ideas

<br>

[Positivist Theories]{.blue}

[Removal of free will]{.blue2}

[Rise of determinalism]{.violet} and scientific explanations of crime

:::

## Determinalism

[The view that all events, including human actions, are shaped by forces outside of individual will or control]{.blue}

<br>

All events, including crime, are caused by prior conditions (biological, psychological)

<br>

Challenges the assumption of free will central to classical theory

## Recap

[Positivism is determinism]{.orange}

<br> 

In other words, in this perspective on crime, [crime is not due to free will or free choice.]{.violet} 

<br> 

If an individual has features, propagated by positivist, that are associated with criminal behavior (e.g., craniometry, IQ testing) that person [will]{.blue} commit a crime

## Physiognomy 

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

:::{.smaller-text}

Claimed to assess personality traits and moral character by [analyzing facial features (e.g., eyes, nose, jaw, mouth)]{.blue}

<br>
Examples: large jaws, forward projection of jaw, how sloping forehead, hard shifty eyes

<br>

Argued that [outward appearance revealed inner qualities or dispositions]{.blue2}

<br>

[Influenced criminology by stigmatizing certain groups based on supposed “criminal” looks]{.blue}

:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

<br>


![](Images/phys.jpeg){.absolute top=50 right=10 height="70%"}

## On the Origin of Species (1859)


::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}

::: {.small-text}

**Charles Darwin**

[Foundation of modern biology and genetics.]{.orange}

Explains species change via [natural selection]{.blue}

<br>

::: {.smaller-text}

Key Points:

[Variation:]{.orange} Genetic differences exist within a population

[Competition:]{.orange} Organisms compete for limited resources

[Adaptation:]{.orange} Beneficial traits improve survival

[Natural Selection:]{.orange} Favorable traits are passed on

[Speciation:]{.orange} Accumulated changes lead to new species

::: 

:::

:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

![](Images/os.jpg){.absolute top=100 right=10 height="70%"}

:::

:::

## Misuse of Darwin's On the Origin of Species

::: {.small-text}

**Francis Galton** created [Social Darwinism]{.orange}

[Misapplied natural selection to human societies, using "survival of the fittest" to justify social inequality and group dominance.]{.blue}

<br>

Claimed intelligence, morality, and criminality were hereditary, [advocating reproduction for the "fit" and restrictions for the "unfit."]{.orange}

<br>

Provided a pseudoscientific basis for discriminatory [policies like forced sterilizations and immigration controls]{.blue2}, framed as improving the human race.

:::

## Lombroso's Theory of Atavism and the "Born Criminal"


::: {.small-text}

The Criminal Man (1876), which propagated [Atavism]{.blue}

[Criminals are evolutionary "throwbacks" to primitive humans, exhibiting physical, mental, and behavioral traits of earlier stages of human development.]{.blue}

<br>


Certain individuals are [biologically predisposed to criminal behavior]{.orange}, identifiable through physical stigmata (e.g., asymmetrical faces, large jaws, sloping foreheads).

<br>

[Pioneered the positivist school of criminology]{.grey}, shifting focus from free will to biological determinism in explaining criminal behavior.

:::

## Intelligence Quotient (IQ)

::: {.small-text}

[Alfred Binet developed IQ testing to identify under performing students]{.orange}, where he had children do tasks such as follow commands, copy patterns, name objects, and put things in order or arrange them properly.

Believed IQ could [change over time]{.blue}

:::

<br>

![](Images/IQ.png){fig-align="center"}

::: footer

Image: Lumen Learning

:::

# WE ARE BACK TO THE PSEUDOSCIENCE!

## IQ and Eugenics


::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.small-text}

[H.H. Goddard]{.blue} took Binet's ideas to propagate eugenic policies.

<br>

Claimed IQ was [static and inherited.]{.orange}

<br>

Introduced the concept of "feeblemindedness" to label individuals with below-average IQ

<br>

Created a ranking system to categorize intelligence levels

:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

![](Images/IQEU.jpg)

:::

:::

::: footer

Image: American Scientist

:::
    
## *Buck v. Bell*

:::{.small-text}

A 1927 Supreme Court case that upheld Virginia's law [allowing the sterilization of Carrie Buck, a woman who was deemed "feeble-minded".]{.blue}

<br>

Her condition had been present in her family for the last three generations. [Justice Holmes declared, “Three generations of imbeciles are enough.”]{.orange}

<br>

This idea led to over [60,000 people sterilized in the U.S.]{.blue2}, mostly women, minorities, and disabled individuals (e.g., 19,000 women were sterilized in California) and lasted until 1970s

<br>

[NPR Podcast](https://www.npr.org/2017/03/24/521360544/the-supreme-court-ruling-that-led-to-70-000-forced-sterilizations)


:::
